results.title: French film star Depardieu drops appeal against sexual conviction
results.content: French film star Gérard Depardieu on Monday dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021 and issued "sincere apologies" for his past behaviour on set. "For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour," Depardieu, 77, said in the statement, withdrawing his appeal on the day it was set to go to trial. "I believed my remarks and some of my gestures would be without consequences" for those involved, he said. "They were not, particularly coming from a powerful figure such as I once was."

results.title: French troops in Ukraine 'wouldn't be a surprise'
results.content: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, France 24's sister radio network Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday. While the deployment has not been confirmed, such a mission would not come as a surprise to many in Ukraine, reports France 24's correspondent in Kyiv Gulliver Cragg.

results.title: Prague: Thousands of Czechs rally against government media funding plan
results.content: Tens of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday, November 15, against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget, a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability.

results.title: Robert Pattinson named as new James Bond
results.content: British actor Robert Pattinson, star of three mega-franchises, "The Batman", "Harry Potter" and "Twilight", has been named as the seventh 007. The announcement ends years of speculation about who would inherit the beloved role from Daniel Craig and comes five years after the last Bond release, "No Time to Die".

results.title: Melissa Auf Der Maur: 90s rock memoirs and photographs
results.content: Melissa Auf Der Maur grew up in Montreal, the daughter of a feminist activist mother and a journalist-turned-politician father. At just 22, she joined Courtney Love’s band Hole as its bass player, going on to become a role model for young female fans – and not only female fans – of alternative rock. She later joined The Smashing Pumpkins before striking out on her own as a solo artist. She dropped by FRANCE 24 to talk to Marjorie Hache about the epic decade that brought the 20th century to a close.

results.title: Verdict due in French trial over triple murder linked to Marseille drug wars
results.content: In France, a highly anticipated verdict in a triple homicide is expected later today. Often called the Kessaci trial, the plight of the Kessaci family has drawn attention across France, the surviving brother Amine Kessaci has become an outspoken advocate against drug trafficking and in particular in Marseille.

results.title: Did France abandon its athletes after the Olympics?
results.content: Two years after hosting the Olympics, France seems to have lost interest in supporting its athletes. With budget cuts and lackluster interest from sponsors, some – despite their competitive successes – are turning to influencer work to finance their sport careers.

results.title: COP31 deal draft foreshadows difficult route to consensus
results.content: COP31 negotiators in Turkey released a draft agreement on Monday to advance talks on fossil fuels and climate finance before this week's deadline. The pressure to reach a deal is intense after a year of environmental challenges including catastrophic glacier flooding in Nepal and European wildfires, even as global conflict and cost-of-living protests distract leaders from climate action.

results.title: Saudi Arabia dismisses commander of anti-Houthi coalition as rebels advance
results.content: Saudi Arabia has removed the commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, state media said Monday, as the Iran-backed rebels advanced on the temporary capital of Aden. The shake up comes after Houthi forces took territory on Yemen's southern coast and Saudi-backed forces fell back to defend the capital.

results.title: 'Historical fiction is about filling in the gaps', author Ian McGuire says
results.content: A Man Booker Prize nominee has been speaking to FRANCE 24 about his latest novel and his passion for researching and writing historical fiction. Ian McGuire was shortlisted for the prize in 2016 for his novel “The North Water”. His latest book, “White River Crossing”, was published earlier this year and has now been translated into French, under the shortened title “White River”.

results.title: Musk among more than 150,000 calling for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
results.content: Could Jensen Huang make a stunning return to Nvidia just days after resigning as CEO of the AI chip giant over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy? The possibility is growing after Elon Musk and more than 158,000 others signed an open letter calling for Huang's reinstatement.

results.title: French troops 'deployed in Ukraine on secret mission'
results.content: French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, France 24's sister radio network Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look at the report's claims.

results.title: Russia says intercepted over 1,300 Ukrainian drones in a major attack
results.content: Russia intercepted 1,336 drones launched by Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Monday, in what was the most claimed downings since Moscow’s all-out invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago. Russia, meanwhile, has battered Ukrainian civilian areas with relentless strikes that seek to choke the economy and break public morale, in attacks President Volodymyr Zelensky said were made possible ⁠partly due to restrictions on Ukraine's use of SpaceX's Starshield service.

results.title: Israel's Netanyahu accused of electoral interference
results.content: Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot said on Sunday caretaker premier Benjamin Netanyahu must leave office immediately following reports of alleged electoral interference by a Netanyahu aide. France 24's Noga Tarnopolsky has the details.

results.title: French presidential election: Should centrists hold a primary to challenge far right and left?
results.content: A growing list of presidential hopefuls are jostling for attention ahead of France's 2027 election, as mainstream candidates seek to derail a showdown between the far right and far left. But with a crowded field splitting the vote, should a primary among centrist candidates? Marc Perelman takes a closer look.

results.title: Iran blocks UN nuclear site visits until war ends
results.content: Iran's foreign ministry on Monday said that it would block the International Atomic Energy Agency's access to its damaged nuclear facilities until stated conditions for permanently ending the war have been met by the US. The ministry's statement follows calls for the UN watchdog to resume inspections of nuclear sites, which have been suspended since last year's 12-day war with Israel.

results.title: Excitement builds ahead of GTA VI release
results.content: After eight years of development by Rockstar Games and multiple delays, the 6th installment of the world's most talked-about game Grand Theft Auto is being released this Thursday, November 19. The game, founded nearly three decades ago and built around stealing cars and outrunning the police, boasts some 500 million sales, and this time is preparing for yet another big score, as millions of fans around the world get ready for its launch.

results.title: Cape Verde President Neves wins second term
results.content: Cape Verde President José Maria Neves has won a second five-year term, according to provisional results from Sunday's election, besting five challengers ​including the archipelago's ‌first female candidate after a campaign focused on the need to create more ⁠jobs for young people.

results.title: Hundreds of thousands protest Czech government's media funding plan
results.content: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget — a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability.

results.title: Pope Leo wraps up South America tour that tested recovery from cancer surgery
results.content: Pope Leo XIV concludes his 12-day homecoming tour of South America on Monday, a visit that has helped dispel concerns over his health following his recovery from cancer surgery. The 71-year-old pontiff visited Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, crisscrossing a continent where he had spent almost two decades serving as a missionary.

results.title: Francophonie summit avoids 'major disaster' after clash over leadership
results.content: A summit of French-speaking nations attended by France's Emmanuel Macron postponed the election of a new chief Monday after a row between African neighbours the Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda. The postponement appears to have staved off a threatened walkout by DR Congo, avoiding what would have been a "major disaster", says France 24's Philip Turle.

results.title: What is the International Organisation of la Francophonie?
results.content: With the 20th Francophonie Summit underway in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, all eyes are on the International Organisation of la Francophonie (OIF). But what is the OIF? Resembling the Commonwealth, this post-colonial bloc unites around 90 nations, from 53 full members to friendly states drawn by political and economic ties. Liza Kaminov breaks down what the organisation is all about.

results.title: Gérard Depardieu: Cinema icon drops appeal and apologises to victims
results.content: French actor Gérard Depardieu on Monday withdrew his appeal against his 2025 conviction for sexual assault, acknowledging his guilt and apologising to his victims. He has also been indicted in a separate case following a rape complaint, with a decision expected on November 26.

results.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after attempted arson attack on drone ‌maker
results.content: Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from December 1, its foreign minister said on Sunday, following a suspected sabotage attack on an Estonian drone maker that Tallinn blamed on Moscow.
